paper_title: Compressibility Barriers to Neighborhood-Preserving Data Visualization
authors: Szymon Snoeck, Noah Bergam, Nakul Verma
statement: criterion, it is worth investigating its interplay with manifold-type inputs. Another natural line of investigation involves approximate α-preservation: given some neighborhood graph and a fixed target dimension d, what fraction of neighborhoods can be α-preserved in d? Does this relaxation dramatically change the stringent lower bounds of this work? If so, then answering this question for real-world datasets would allow us calibrate our expectations for data visualization on a case-bycase basis. Finally, it is tempting to pursue an algorithmic realization of α-preservation. Our study of α-preservation suggests that certain efficiently computable graph statistics, including C(G) and the graph spectrum, can help to quantify α-preservation dimension.
